Given the latent trajectory { z t } \{z_{t}\} generated by the SDE, I define the observation model through a conditional likelihood function p ψ ​ ( x t | z t ) p_{\psi}(x_{t}|z_{t}) . In its simplest form, this is modeled as a multivariate Gaussian with mean given by a neural network decoder f ψ ​ ( z t ) f_{\psi}(z_{t}) and a fixed isotropic variance: where f ψ : ℝ d → ℝ n f_{\psi}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{n} maps the latent state to the data space, and σ 2 \sigma^{2} is a scalar parameter. This formulation is standard in variational autoencoders ( [ 23 ] ), and it allows for tractable computation of the log-likelihood and its gradients during training. The neural decoder f ψ f_{\psi} is typically implemented as a multi-layer perceptron or convolutional network, depending on the data modality. For instance, in image-based tasks, convolutional architectures provide inductive biases such as translation equivariance and locality ( [ 16 ] ), while for time series or structured signals, recurrent or attention-based architectures may better capture autocorrelations ( [ 13 ] ). In more complex settings, the assumption of fixed variance may be overly restrictive.
